name: pdk-elsa-external-callbacks-exactly-once
instr:
A suspended `RunTask` can strand an approval if its `Elsa.RunTask` webhook meets an unavailable receiver. HTTP Endpoint resumes currently execute outside the distributed runtime lock, so two nodes can continue the same bookmark twice.

In `/app`, make the workbench host's external hand-offs cluster-safe:

- A `RunTask` creates one task ID and a durable delivery for **each configured sink** when its workflow state commits. Deliver `Elsa.RunTask` with the existing `taskId`, `taskName`, and `workflowInstanceId` payload fields. Send an `X-Elsa-Delivery-Id` header stable for a given task and sink across attempts. Retry non-2xx responses or connection failures; begin the first retry within 10 seconds. After a 20-second receiver outage, every task must arrive within 30 seconds of recovery without a second task ID. A node killed after suspension but before delivery must not lose the task: another node delivers it within 45 seconds. Sinks accept a delivery on 2xx; never require a receiver to make exactly one HTTP request under a lost acknowledgement.
- A suspended HTTP Endpoint bookmark under `/workflows/{path}` continues at most once, including ten concurrent POSTs split between two nodes. One resume succeeds with 200; competing requests receive 409 or 404, without repeating downstream effects. Task completion racing an HTTP resume on separate nodes for the same instance must preserve both steps without rerunning either. Preserve normal non-concurrent HTTP routing and the completion
